script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union for Monday, November 2. Here is the week's news.

Lake Elmo's Planning Commission met Monday on a variance for a new eight hundred seventy-two square foot detached garage at eleven thousand fifty-five Thirty-second Street North.

Doug and Kelly Biever want to construct the garage, remove the existing five hundred seventy-nine square foot structure and other impervious surface, and relocate the driveway. The lot is zero point six acres zoned Rural Single Family with a Shoreland Overlay. City code sets a maximum impervious surface coverage of twenty-five percent. The property already exceeds that limit: thirty point nine percent now, after earlier renovations that left it at thirty-two point nine percent and thirty-three point eight percent before that.

Staff recommends approval with conditions that keep the finished coverage at twenty-eight point six percent and require the existing impervious to be removed first. The variance would expire if work does not start within twelve months.

The commission met at six-thirty in the evening at thirty-eight eighty Laverne Avenue North.

Stillwater's Parks and Recreation Commission met Monday night on a covered outdoor hockey rink for the Stillwater Area Hockey Association and approval of a new park sign design.

The agenda also included a presentation on the Land and Water Legacy Referendum from Washington County and unfinished business on the Lumberjack Landing Guiding Document.

The commission met at seven in the evening.

Oakdale's council workshop Tuesday took up a proposed twenty-two million one hundred forty-three thousand three hundred forty-four dollar property-tax levy for twenty twenty-seven, an eight point nine seven percent increase of one million eight hundred twenty-three thousand six hundred sixteen dollars.

The general fund accounts for one million one hundred sixty-three thousand eight hundred fifty-one dollars of the rise, the capital improvement program five hundred twenty-three thousand dollars, and debt service one hundred sixty-nine thousand seven hundred sixty-five dollars. A median residential property valued at three hundred fifty-two thousand dollars would see about one hundred ten dollars and forty-two cents more a year, or nine dollars and twenty cents a month. Low-volume residential utility bills would rise two dollars and sixty-four cents a month and high-volume bills eight dollars and forty-eight cents.

The workshop also covered a utility rate study, the proposed twenty twenty-seven fee schedule, and the capital improvement plan. The vehicle and equipment replacement fund levy would be one million one hundred thousand dollars. The municipal building fund would rise to five hundred ninety-three thousand dollars.

Truth-in-Taxation is set for December eight at seven in the evening, the same night the final levy would be adopted.

The workshop started at five at the Discovery Center, forty-four forty-four Hadley Avenue North.

Oakdale's council met Tuesday on a public hearing to certify two hundred forty-eight thousand five hundred three dollars and seventy-five cents in delinquent utilities and inactive accounts onto twenty twenty-seven property taxes.

Three hundred two accounts make up the total, including interest and a thirty-five dollar certification fee on each. Remaining balances would be levied with five point seven five percent interest. Payments are accepted until November fifteen.

The same night the council took up a one hundred forty-one thousand two hundred eighty dollar professional services agreement with KLM Engineering for Water Tower four reconditioning, a one hundred sixty-seven thousand four hundred fifty-two dollar and seventy-five cent change order for Walton Park parking lot work on the police expansion and city hall remodel, and claims of five million six hundred eighty-five thousand forty-four dollars and seven cents covering October fourteen through twenty-seven.

A joint powers agreement would let the owner of property at forty-four fifty-five Olson Lake Trail pay a twenty-five thousand eight hundred sixty-nine dollar lateral benefit charge for sanitary sewer.

The meeting was at seven at the Discovery Center, forty-four forty-four Hadley Avenue North.

Stillwater Area Public Schools board met Tuesday on high school course proposals for twenty twenty-seven through twenty twenty-eight and on demolishing the Old Lake Elmo School Building.

The course report covers expanded college credit, career pathways, and online learning, with one-time and ongoing costs and grant funding. Specific dollar figures are not printed in the agenda summary.

The demolition item would remove the building, underground infrastructure, and site amenities, grade the property, add topsoil, and seed it. The work is contingent on City of Lake Elmo approval.

Consent items include a five hundred dollar grant and a two-year agreement with Salem Lutheran School for middle school wrestling.

The meeting was at five-thirty in the evening. The agenda does not print a location.

Stillwater's planning commission met Wednesday night on a zoning change that would let accessory structures reach one thousand square feet on parcels of fifty thousand square feet or more in the Traditional Residential district.

Daniel Garrity wants a one thousand square foot accessory structure at twelve thousand two hundred ten McKusick Road, on top of a proposed attached garage. Current rules cap an attached garage plus all accessory structures at one thousand square feet or ten percent of the net developable area, whichever is less. An accessory structure itself is limited to five hundred square feet, or seven hundred twenty when no garage is attached. Staff proposes the larger allowance and a one thousand five hundred square foot combined maximum for those big lots. The property is about one point seven acres. Only three parcels would be affected. The application was complete September twenty-one. The sixty-day deadline is November twenty.

Gina and Dan Sedlacek appeal the staff view that a pool is an accessory structure, and therefore barred, at twelve thirty-four Macey Way in Settler's Glen. City code says accessory structures are not allowed in the Cove Cottage Residential district. Three existing pools in Settlers Glen were approved administratively in the last five years.

Staff will also discuss land use and density for the twenty fifty comprehensive plan. Forecasts put population at twenty-two thousand five hundred in twenty fifty, up from nineteen thousand three hundred ninety-four in twenty twenty.

The commission met at seven in the evening at two hundred sixteen Fourth Street North.

Stillwater's city council meets Tuesday night on a Myrtle Street reconstruction estimated at four million five hundred seventy thousand one hundred forty-two dollars and a five hundred dollar service charge on downtown commercial buildings.

The Myrtle Street Improvement Project runs from Owens Street North to Main Street North, zero point seven two miles. The feasibility report puts the total at four million five hundred seventy thousand one hundred forty-two dollars, including design, surveying, inspection, administration, and contingencies. Assessments on benefiting properties total six hundred seventy thousand one hundred forty-two dollars, or thirty-five percent under the assessment policy, with the city funding the other sixty-five percent. A state LRIP grant covers one million four hundred thousand dollars and state aid funds cover two million five hundred thousand dollars. Residential owners would pay seven thousand eight hundred four dollars per unit. Corner lots count as half a unit per frontage. Duplexes and condominiums count as zero point eight units. Commercial, city, and church-owned properties would pay one hundred eighty-five dollars per adjusted linear foot. An appraisal estimated a twelve thousand dollar benefit per residential unit. The council will hold a public hearing and consider a resolution to order the improvements.

Downtown, the Special Service District would collect fifty thousand five hundred dollars for services, or five hundred dollars per commercial building inside the district. One property is listed at one thousand dollars. The charges are payable with twenty twenty-six taxes in one installment at zero interest. The payment deadline is November sixteen, twenty twenty-six; any remaining balance goes to the county as a special assessment. Only commercial property in the district is subject to the charges. Staff recommends holding a public hearing and adopting the assessments.

Tax Increment Financing District number eight, decertified as of December thirty-one, twenty twenty-two, has two hundred ninety-one thousand eight hundred ninety-seven dollars and ninety-one cents in excess increment. Staff recommends remitting it to Washington County for redistribution to local taxing entities.

A zoning text amendment for accessory structures in the Traditional Residential district is on for first reading. The planning commission unanimously recommended it on October twenty-eight. Staff says it would let larger lots put up bigger structures, up to one thousand square feet, while limiting the effect on average TR properties. One example is a parcel at twelve thousand two hundred ten McKusick Road.

The Greater Stillwater Chamber of Commerce seeks an agreement for the twenty twenty-seven World Snow Celebration and asks to waive fees totaling thirty-nine thousand one hundred fifty dollars. An ice rink agreement includes a request to waive eighteen thousand five hundred dollars in fees. The tipping fee would be one hundred fifty-nine dollars per ton.

The meeting is scheduled for seven in the evening on November four.

Times and documents are in the show notes.
